title: Etale cohomology of a strictly henselian local scheme vanishes in positive degrees
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then the global sections functor $\Gamma(S,-):\Ab(S_{\Et})\to\textit{Ab}$ on abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] is exact, and $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal F)=0$ for every $\mathcal F\in\Ab(S_{\Et})$ and every $p\ge1$ (etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]).

proof.text: Install the strictly henselian instance from hR. The already proved source-library instance Scheme.preservesEpimorphisms_sheafSections_of_isStrictlyHenselianLocalRing (WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.StrictlyHenselian, Stacks 03QO) says that sections at the identity etale object preserve epimorphisms. Its proof constructs sections of etale neighbourhoods over the closed point, so every covering sieve there contains the identity. Transport this property to global sections by Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections and Functor.PreservesEpimorphisms.of_iso. Global sections are additive and preserve finite limits as a right adjoint. Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels then gives preservation of kernels and cokernels, and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology gives finite colimits. Conclude exactFunctor_iff.

proof.text: For an exact additive functor G, the proved source-library natural isomorphism G.rightDerivedFunctorHomologyFunctorIso p identifies G applied to H^p(K) with H^p(RG(K)). It is built from the exact-functor complex-cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], descent to the derived category, and uniqueness of right derived functors (Functor.rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.MapDerivedCategory). Take K = F[0]. It is concentrated in degree zero, so DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE gives H^p(K) = 0 for p >= 1. The additive functor G preserves zero objects. Transfer this zero object through the comparison isomorphism to H^p(RG(F[0])), which is the etale cohomology object by definition.
